name: Kwame Nkrumah
role: Prime Minister (1952-1960) and first President (1960-1966) of Ghana; Pan-Africanist theorist
summary: Nkrumah led the Gold Coast to independence in 1957 and governed Ghana as a self-described socialist nationalist, using state planning and state enterprises. He advocated a continental Union Government of Africa, non-alignment and opposition to neo-colonialism, held to Marxist class analysis, and after 1964 ruled through a one-party state. After his 1966 overthrow he argued for armed revolution across Africa.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said the age of socialised planning means production and distribution are governed by social needs, not by chaos, greed and self-interest; argued capitalism rests on exploitation.

public-ownership.rationale: Held that the major means of production and distribution ought to be socialised; as president built State farms, factories and corporations and said state enterprises would supply the bulk of revenue.

unions-good.rationale: Urged colonial workers to organise and demanded trade union and strike rights in the 1945 Pan-African declaration; later restructured the TUC under party guidance, so support was for unions allied to the party.

property-fundamental.rationale: Called capitalism domestic colonialism and wanted major means of production socialised, though he assured peasants their individual farms would not be subordinated to State farms.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wrote that foreign capital must operate under a national plan set by the host government and described monopolies as dominating weaker states; did not exclude foreign investment.

central-planning.rationale: Introduced comprehensive economic plans (Seven-Year Development Plan, 1964) because piecemeal 'shopping list' projects were too slow; presented planning as the socialist method.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Required that foreign investment follow a national plan and directed investment through State enterprises and the Volta and industrial projects.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Described Ghana's aim as a socialist society in which each gives according to ability and receives according to needs.

production-for-use.rationale: Told the OAU that the age of socialised planning means production and distribution are governed by social needs rather than greed and self-interest.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Wrote that capitalism's essential principle is exploitation, calling it 'the gentleman's method of slavery'; Class Struggle in Africa treats surplus extraction by the bourgeoisie as exploitation.

collective-farming.rationale: Promoted State farms and co-operatives but stated they were not alternatives to peasant farming and that individual peasant farmers would not be subordinated to them.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Argued in Towards Colonial Freedom that under imperialism war cannot be averted because of the struggle over colonies and spheres of influence.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defended and instituted the one-party State (1964), calling it suited to African socialist society, with the CPP as vanguard guided by scientific socialism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposed federal and separatist demands in the Gold Coast and condemned the Katanga secession, calling the Congo indivisible.

political-violence-never.rationale: In 1966-68 wrote that non-violent methods are now anachronistic and that armed struggle is the highest form of political action in the neo-colonial situation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wrote that in Africa the state must be secular, though not at war with religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Insisted on a secular state and called religion an instrument of bourgeois social reaction.

more-religion-public.rationale: Argued religion is used by colonialists and opportunists to divert people from secular concerns and that the state must be secular.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Said insistence on a secular state is not a political declaration of war on religion, which must be understood before it can be tackled.

religion-illusion.rationale: Wrote that religion is rooted in poverty and fear ('fear created the gods') and serves reaction, but did not predict it would simply fade.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Repudiated tribal chauvinism and racial prejudice and sought a union of many African peoples; Ghana's CPP excluded tribalism and racialism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Consciencism and Class Struggle in Africa present class conflict arising from productive forces as the driver of social change.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Wrote that the conflict between classes is shaped by development of productive forces and technology, and that socialism rests on dialectical and historical materialism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said any meaningful humanism must begin from egalitarianism and lead to policies that safeguard it, while speaking in terms of equal opportunities for development.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Told the UN that African nationalism challenges colonial powers to make just restitution for years of injustice and crime committed against the continent.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Contrasted socialised planning driven by social needs with systems governed by greed and self-interest.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Said that in the age of science and technology poverty, ignorance and disease are retreating foes and that science could make even the Sahara bloom.

revolution-justified.rationale: Wrote that the passage from capitalism to socialism can only lie through revolution, and later advocated armed revolution in Africa.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejected a return to pre-colonial society as unworthy of African efforts; the way out is only forward to socialism.

gradual-change.rationale: Held that reform keeps fundamental principles constant and only revolution can pass from capitalism to socialism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Built policy on an explicit ideology (Consciencism, scientific socialism) while warning socialism must adapt to local conditions.

direct-action.rationale: Led the Positive Action strikes and boycotts of 1949-50 but also built a mass party that contested elections.

vanguard-party.rationale: Described the CPP as the conscious political vanguard and called for a vanguard revolutionary party to educate and lead workers and peasants.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: CPP constitution required members to accept the party's policy, programme and discipline, and decisions had to be loyally executed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wrote the 1945 Pan-African declaration affirming the right of all peoples to govern themselves.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Told the UN the organisation must determine what is lawful and enforce it, and proposed a permanent African seat on the Security Council.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Campaigned for a continental Union Government of Africa as essential to independence.

open-borders.rationale: Said African unity would render existing boundaries obsolete and urged breaking down the barriers dividing Africans; this concerned African states, not borders generally.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pursued 'positive neutralism and non-alignment' as Ghana's foreign policy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Urged that African states annul foreign bases and military pacts with outside powers.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Told the UN he supported measures to prevent foreign military bases on African soil and urged powers to give up bases.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Proposed that nuclear powers keep Africa out of their nuclear plans and bar states with nuclear weapons from African bases.

arms-reduction.rationale: Told the UN it is ridiculous to pile up arms and tied world prosperity to disarmament.

people-in-arms.rationale: Handbook envisages professional armies disappearing and Africa defended by a continental people's militia.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Wrote that between an awakening zone and a contested zone only a handful of genuine revolutionaries prepared to organise and act is missing.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Handbook proposed a continental force that would supply equipment and cadres to partisan units fighting neo-colonial governments.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Called colonial boundaries artificial and obsolete yet opposed secession inside existing states such as Congo and Ghana.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Said artificial colonial boundaries must be broken down to give viable economic units and ultimately a single African unit.

dominated-front.rationale: Advocated non-alignment and African, Asian and Afro-Asian solidarity against imperialism and neo-colonialism.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Neo-Colonialism argues foreign capital in less developed countries exploits rather than develops them, widening the gap between rich and poor states.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Argued that nominal independence without economic control is neo-colonialism and that real independence requires economic independence.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Told the UN that inequality between developed and under-developed countries could cause an international explosion.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Warned that aid is a tool of neo-colonialism when it carries conditions, while also calling for development assistance through the UN; evidence points both ways.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Described aid and assistance bodies as vehicles of neo-colonial control and stressed national plans and continental development.

national-resource-control.rationale: Wrote that Africa's resources exploited with foreign capital enrich foreign investors, and sought national control of the economy through State enterprises.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Argued capitalism's devices could not cope with recurrent crises and that neo-colonialism's contradictions make its collapse certain.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejected capitalism and described socialism and communism as restatements of communalist principles in modern form.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Cited the Soviet Union as the world's first socialist state and received the Lenin Peace Prize.

defeat-communism.rationale: Allied Ghana with socialist states, said socialism is an international idea, and attacked anti-communism as neo-colonialist propaganda.

class-collaboration.rationale: Treated the African bourgeoisie as allied with imperialism and class struggle as central to the African revolution.

independent-unions.rationale: Described the party as the conscious political vanguard of the trade union movement and reorganised the TUC under that guidance.

workers-own-party.rationale: Wanted the national liberation movement rooted in labour, farmers and youth and built the CPP on that base.

corporate-influence.rationale: Documented in Neo-Colonialism how large corporations and financial interests shape the policies of states.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Held that each person is an end in himself and not merely a means, with equal opportunities for development.

person-over-state.rationale: Wrote that each man is an end in himself, not a means, while detaining opponents without trial under the Preventive Detention Act; mixed.

positive-liberty.rationale: The 1945 declaration listed freedom from poverty and economic exploitation among the three freedoms of national liberation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Wrote of sovereignty vested in the masses, but made Ghana a one-party state, became president for life and detained opponents without trial; the record wins.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Proposed the 1964 amendment making him president for life of nation and party.

term-limits.rationale: Proposed the 1964 amendment making him president for life.

leader-cult.rationale: Reference accounts say a cult of personality grew around him and he used the title Osagyefo; contested as to his role.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Introduced the Preventive Detention Act and told the Assembly that the need for it still remained.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Condemned apartheid and racialism, and said Ghana pressed for South Africa's expulsion from the ILO.

racial-franchise.rationale: Demanded one man one vote and majority rule in Rhodesia.

property-franchise.rationale: Demanded universal franchise in Rhodesia and democracy by one man one vote.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Stated biologists maintain there is no 'superior' race and that people are products of environment.

character-from-environment.rationale: Wrote that men and women are as much products of environment as of instinct and heredity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rejected the colonial claim of a civilising mission, saying Europeans used it as a cloak to rob Africa.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned colonial economies as arranged for the benefit of the metropolitan power.

racial-pride.rationale: Promoted the African personality and in 1968 supported Black Power as a vanguard movement for people of African descent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Called for restitution for colonial injustice and supported Black Power's demand for redress in 1968.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Argued Africans share history and interests and should unite, though on continental rather than language-family grounds.

civilizational-union.rationale: Urged political union of African states on the basis of shared history and common interest.

decide-locally.rationale: Insisted on a unitary state, called federalism a red herring, and devolved only limited powers to regions.

second-chamber.rationale: The CPP opposed an upper house for chiefs sought by the opposition.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Shifted power from chiefs to elected councils and had hostile chiefs destooled, criticising chieftaincy.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The CPP wanted regional assemblies to be more or less advisory and kept devolved powers dependent on Accra.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Backed UN and African forces to end the Katanga secession and eliminate private armies in the Congo.

party-own-road.rationale: Said socialism does not belong to the Soviet Union or China and that each state's policies take particular forms from its circumstances.

non-intervention.rationale: Condemned neo-colonial interference yet urged UN and African intervention in the Congo and armed aid to liberation movements.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Called for permanent delimitation of Israel and a UN-mediated settlement, while criticising Israeli action in 1967.

women-suffrage.rationale: CPP constitution gave women no separate status within the party, and his government reserved parliamentary seats for women in 1959-60.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Pursued rapid industrialisation as the route to development and called it central to ending poverty.
